config.note: No fault injected. The trigger is a DUPLICATE create: POST the same contact (same accountId + documentNumber business key) twice. The unmodified SUT's dedupe path soft-rejects the second create.

injection.trigger_input: POST an identical contact twice in a row (second call is the case)

ground_truth.label: negative
ground_truth.rationale: Designed duplicate-rejection, not a lost write: the second create returns HTTP 2xx with a TrainTicket envelope carrying status:0 ('already exists' semantics) and by design persists nothing. The surface phenomenon matches accept-then-drop (2xx + absent from read-back), which is why this is the canonical benign trap for the acknowledged-lost-write class on this SUT - but the response body explicitly signals non-acceptance (status:0), so a correct ack rule must exclude it. Grounded in the Gate-1 G0 evidence (prep/sut-fault-injection-capability.md section 9; the ACCEPT_THEN_DROP_DISCLOSURE in PairedFaultExecutor documents that TrainTicket's only by-design drop soft-rejects with status:0).

provenance.notes: Stratum-2 benign trap for the ack rule specifically: mist_dataintegrity must NOT fire because its acknowledgement predicate (2xx AND body status in {null,1}) excludes the status:0 soft-reject - the write is not acknowledged, so the base relation is vacuous (a true negative, NOT a false positive avoided by luck). body_marker_oracle FLAGS the status:0 marker and is therefore WRONG on this case (the rejection is intended business behavior, not a fault) - that gap is the discriminating value of the case. The case also documents the disclosed limitation that TrainTicket has NO representative of the 2xx-accepted-but-never-persists trap class whose body claims success (the only by-design drop signals status:0), per the ACCEPT_THEN_DROP_DISCLOSURE shipped in the pairing report.
